answer_1.quote: We evaluate 4 leading proprietary LLMs, 11 popular open-source general LLMs and 5 open-source code LLMs on CoV-Eval benchmark ... The benchmark consists of four evaluation tasks: code completion, vulnerability repair, vulnerability detection, and vulnerability classification.
answer_1.outputs: Generated code snippets for code completion, vulnerability repair, detection, and classification tasks.

answer_2.quote: In the CoV-Eval benchmark, we adopt the "Security Rate (SR)" as the evaluation metric for both code completion and vulnerability repair tasks ... we also report pass@1 scores of various LLMs on HumanEval ... For discrimination tasks (vulnerability detection and classification), we compute the weighted F1 score, recall and accuracy.

answer_3.quote: We developed an improved judgment model, VC-Judge, which aligns better with human expertise, enabling more reliable security evaluation of LLM-generated codes in CoV-Eval ... VC-Judge is used after generation to determine whether LLM-generated codes contain specific types of vulnerabilities.
methods: LLM-based judgment with direct w/o analysis prompt

answer_4.quote: We asked three master students to annotate vulnerabilities for 216 selected LLM-generated programs ... The final labels were determined by majority voting among the three annotators. If all three annotators provided different results, a PhD student conducted a review to finalize the label.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators determined whether the given code snippets contained vulnerabilities and, if so, identified the types of vulnerabilities.
